subject: Dedicated capacity: tactical shoulder & burst cadence for Mintara Therapeutics
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@mintara.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@mintara.ai>
Date: 2028-07-28T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing + burst terms

Rishi —

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re close to committing but need a tighter picture on how Redwood would support our two operating modes: (1) latency-sensitive inference during business hours (US/EU overlap) and (2) nightly model refreshes / fine-tuning windows that create heavy, sustained GPU load.

Quick facts from our side (attached CSV):
- Daily token volume: ~1.8M tokens/day (varies)
- Peak concurrent inference sessions: ~1,200 (short spikes)
- Nightly training window: 00:00-04:00 UTC, sustained GPU utilization up to 80% for 3–4 hours

We need to lock in: reserved slab sizing, shoulder capacity to absorb short spikes, clear soft/hard-burst definitions and any credit/penalty language for capacity limits. Can you share a concrete proposal and an example autoscale policy (timings/thresholds) that matches our traffic?

Also looping in procurement for timing — procurement@mintara.ai.

Thanks,
Alex
Principal ML Engineer
Mintara Therapeutics

Attachment: Mintara_usage_snapshot_July.csv (CSV, 46KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@mintara.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@mintara.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-28T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing + burst terms

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the CSV. Attached is an initial, pragmatic plan to start the conversation (see Dedicated_Capacity_Proposal_Mintara_v1.pdf and SOW draft). High-level proposal: 

- Reserved slab: 16x A100-80GB reserved (primary inference slab). Designed to hold persistent KV cache for your production models and serve latency-critical traffic.
- Shoulder / soft-burst: 6x preemptible A100s in a nearby shoulder pool that can be routed to Mintara with low-latency routing. Soft-burst allowed up to +40% above reserved for windows up to 6 hours (automatic, subject to queueing if adjacent tenants are heavy).
- Hard-burst: up to 24 total GPUs (reserved + ephemeral) for short emergency bursts; hard-burst requires a 2-hour advance notice where possible or will be best-effort during major platform contention.
- Autoscale policy (example): min_instances=16, max_instances=24, scale_up_threshold=70% sustained for 120s, scale_down_threshold=30% sustained for 300s, cooldown=300s. Warm-standby pre-warm for 5min when ramping to hard-burst.
- Credits / failover: if hard-burst cannot be served due to region-wide exhaustion, we propose a 15% service credit (pro-rated) on the affected token consumption for that billing day; alternatively, we can route non-critical jobs to hosted smaller models (rwd-small) automatically as fallback.

Next steps: 1) internal alignment on SLOs & headroom, 2) finalize numbers and DocuSign SOW, 3) plan a 1-hour ops walkthrough to lock autoscale knobs.

I’ve cc’d Neha and Kimberly — they’ll add sizing and runtime notes.

—Rishi
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Dedicated_Capacity_Proposal_Mintara_v1.pdf (PDF, 112KB); SOW_burst_terms.docx (DOCX, 38KB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-29T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: internal: Mintara sizing notes

Quick internal notes after I parsed the CSV:
- The daily token shape supports an always-on inference slab around 14–18 GPUs; 16 is a reasonable starting point. Nightly train spikes look like a sustained 3–4 hour window at ~75–85% of a 16-GPU slab — that drives the soft-burst sizing.
- Recommendation: keep reserved=16, shoulder=6 (preemptible), hard-cap target=24. That gives ~40% soft-burst headroom and a ~50% potential uplift to hard-burst.
- Autoscale tuning:
  * scale_up: >70% avg GPU util across slab for 120s => add +1 GPU unit (or route additional GPU-backed workers)
  * scale_down: <35% avg for 300s => remove -1 unit
  * warmup: 5min to get KV cache rehydrated; recommend the client accept a conservative SLA for cold-started tasks during hard-burst (we flag those explicitly).
- Contractwise: define soft-burst as automatic, up to 6h contiguous windows, no extra charge if <= agreed monthly soft-burst budget (we’ll propose a 10% monthly soft-burst allowance). Hard-burst billed at on-demand premium rate; if platform cannot provide hard-burst, apply agreed credit (see Rishi).

I’ll prep a short table of utilization vs recommended headroom to attach to the proposal.

-Neha
Product Manager, Dedicated Services
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-29T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: internal: infra constraints + KV cache note

Couple of engineering constraints / suggestions to include in the SOW and ops playbook:
- KV cache stickiness: to keep inference latency low during bursts we should ensure the shoulder pool can be populated with warmed KV caches where possible. That implies scheduled pre-warm windows and small snapshot restores (2–5 minutes) when we scale up.
- Batching behavior: if Mintara spikes are short <60s we recommend increasing request-level priority and keeping batch sizes small to preserve tail latency. For multi-minute sustained spikes, larger batching is economical.
- Warm-standby nodes: recommend we maintain 1–2 hot standbys (not billed as full reserved but as a low-cost standby) to reduce 1st-request cold starts during sudden spikes; include these as a line item in proposal.
- Telemetry: add per-route token-level latency, percentiles (p50/p95/p99), and per-GPU utilization dashboards. Link to instrumentation: https://na1.redwood.app/ops/mintara/telemetry (internal).

Kimberly
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@mintara.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@mintara.ai>, procurement@mintara.ai
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing + burst terms — proposal and next steps

Alex / Samir / Procurement —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled this together. Attached is the consolidated proposal and a draft SOW that captures the technical and commercial guardrails we discussed. TL;DR of the proposed commercial/ops terms: 

- Reserved: 16x A100-80GB (primary inference slab, KV cache preserved).
- Shoulder (soft-burst): 6x A100-80GB (preemptible), automatic soft-burst up to +40% for contiguous windows up to 6 hours; monthly soft-burst allowance = 10% of committed tokens (overage free within allowance).
- Hard-burst: up to 24 GPUs total (reserved + ephemeral). Hard-burst is best-effort; we require a 2-hour notice to guarantee placement. If we can’t satisfy the requested hard-burst due to regional exhaustion, Mintara receives a service credit equal to 15% of the affected token spend for that day, or an option to route non-critical jobs to smaller hosted model(s) at no charge for the interruption window.
- Autoscale policy (example that we will implement in the console): min=16, max=24, scale_up=70% sustained for 120s, scale_down=35% sustained for 300s, cooldown=300s, warm-standby=2 nodes, pre-warm=5 minutes before ramp.
- Operational: daily token/latency dashboard, weekly capacity review for the first 90 days, and a 1-hour kickoff ops workshop after SOW signature.

Next steps:
1) Procurement to review SOW (SOW_burst_terms.docx attached) and confirm any redlines or PO cadence.
2) If agreed, sign SOW via DocuSign (link in the attached proposal and HubSpot deal).
3) Schedule the ops walkthrough (I propose Thurs 08/01 10:00 AM PT — cc’d Neha & Kimberly to run technical parts).

Please reply with any redlines or confirm and we’ll push the SOW for signature.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
